items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: I made friends with the old man Lehmann... Mr. Lehmann used to save them for me.

ctx.x: So on the job, if they got a new number to play, I knew it. They'd all say, hey, Scottie, where did you get that? How do you know this number? I wouldn't tell them. I said, I heard it, you know, like that. We lived uptown then, 131st Street, and 135th Street there was Lehmann's Music Shop. Well, to get all the accessories like mutes for my trumpet, and like that, I stopped there instead of having to go downtown.
I made friends with the old man Lehmann, the place is still there now, but it's mostly a card shop. The old man is dead, and his sons took over. He knew I was a musician, because
most of the time I was in a tuxedo. I used to come from high school, change my clothes, put on a tuxedo and then meet the fellows at the Amsterdam.
